newsitem.title: USA: Riscorp to restructure, reduce work force.
newsitem.headline: Riscorp to restructure, reduce work force.

text.p: Insurance company Riscorp Inc. said Thursday it will reduce its work force by 17 percent as part of a reorganization to refocus its operations and reduce expenses.
The company said it plans to refocus its operations around its core managed workers' compensation insurance business.
It said it stopped writing new business owners' policies as of June 1 for a property casualty line it entered in January 1996.

In all, the move will eliminate about 141 positions, including 59 employees and management personnel in its Sarasota headquarters. Prior to the reductions, Riscorp employed 516 people in its Sarasota headquarters and 836 companywide.
In the near-term, Riscorp's total annual payroll and payroll expenses will be reduced by about $9.9 million, or nearly 28 percent.

Moving forward, the company will conduct an ongoing evaluation to reduce overall expenses on a continuing basis. However, Riscorp said it does not currently expect to make any further personnel reductions.

As part of the reorganization, Riscorp said it will consolidate operations into three regional offices: Sarasota, servicing Florida; Birmingham, servicing Alabama; and Charlotte, servicing North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.
Effective July 1997, the company will close its offices in Ft. Lauderdale, Fla.; Montgomery, Ala.; Oklahoma City, Okla.; Kansas City, Kan.; Atlanta; and Richmond.

The company said it plans to maintain its current business and insurance licenses in Oklahoma, Kansas, Missouri and Virginia until those policies expire but will write no new business in those states.
Riscorp stock was up 12.5 cents at $3.50 in morning trading on Nasdaq.
